### 🐛 Describe the bug We are observing degraded grounding accuracy when running Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct model with vLLM versions 0.11.1 and 0.11.2. The model's grounding capabilities (spatial understanding and object localization) show significant precision degradation compared to previous vLLM versions. The model produces incorrect bounding box coordinates and poor spatial reasoning results. ### Reproduction Deploy Code ``` nohup python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --model Qwen/Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct-FP8 --served-model-name qwen3-vl-235b-a22b-instruct --max-model-len 64K --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --trust-remote-code --max-num-seqs 16 --dtype bfloat16 --enable-log-requests --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --async-scheduling --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --enable-expert-parallel --limit-mm-per-prompt.video 0 --mm_encoder_tp_mode="data" --mm_processor_cache_type="shm" & ``` ### Expected Behavior - Accurate bounding box coordinates ([x1, y1, x2, y2] format) - Precise spatial relationship descriptions - Consistent object localization ### Actual Behavior (vLLM 0.11.1/0.11.2) - Incorrect or invalid bounding box coordinates - Poor spatial reasoning accuracy - Inconsistent grounding results compared to vLLM 0.11.0 or direct Hugging Face implementation ### vllm 0.11.1/0.11.2 Grounding ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa8c4dd9-a3e0-4c26-be9d-b18c6739d94d) vllm 0.11.0 Grounding ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e126168c-b635-40bf-b8ed-46b5b68bd0a9) The issue is reproducible with both FP8 quantization and standard precision ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

> > Interesting... `--enforce-eager` seems to fix the problem on `v0.11.1` too, which I'm using. So the problem is with cuda graphs?

> If this is true it means there's something wrong with our language cuda graph impl in 0.11.1 since the vision part is not part of main LM execution pipeline.
> 
> [@420516460](https://github.com/420516460) are you able to verify this as well? That would be great information for us to confirm. Thanks!

Thanks in advance!

comments.author: participant18
comments.body:
**Confirming this bug on Blackwell (GB10 / DGX Spark, sm_121, aarch64) — plus a workaround that keeps CUDA graphs.**

@participant16 asked above whether Blackwell is affected — yes, it is.

**Environment**
- NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), aarch64
- `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.23.0` image: torch 2.11.0+cu130, triton 3.6.0
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct` — affected with on-the-fly FP8 **and** bf16, so it's precision-independent

**Symptom** (same as this thread): with default compilation, Qwen3-VL's pointing/bbox coordinates come back shifted **~0.14 of the image height upward**. Measured on a fixed frame against a target at a known position: compiled dy ≈ −0.14 vs eager dy ≈ 0.00 (eager matches Ollama on the same frame). `--enforce-eager` fixes it, as others here found.

**Workaround that avoids the full eager penalty:** since the root cause is in inductor's triton-compiled kernels — not CUDA-graph capture — running with

```
--compilation-config '{"mode": 0, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL"}'
```

keeps every kernel eager (the buggy codegen never runs) while still capturing/replaying full CUDA graphs for decode. Verified on the GB10: **coordinates are identical to `--enforce-eager`, point-for-point**, on (a) a synthetic exact-ground-truth image (a red square at a known rect — the returned point matches its center) and (b) a real camera frame across 4 different pointing targets. Decode is ~4.5% faster than `--enforce-eager` (3.30 s vs 3.46 s for the same ~400-token grounding request).

So as of `v0.23.0` (torch 2.11 / triton 3.6.0), the regression is still present on Blackwell sm_121, and `cudagraph_mode: FULL` with compilation mode 0 is a coordinate-safe middle ground for anyone stuck on `--enforce-eager`.
